Triangular number (Tn​=n(n+1)/2)

Words: 30
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
A triangular number counts objects arranged in rows of lengths 1,2,…,n. Pairing that sum with its reverse gives Tn​=n(n+1)/2. The identity Tn+12​−Tn2​=(n+1)3 then telescopes to ∑r=1n​r3=Tn2​.

Geometric mean (G=(x1​⋯xn​)1/n)

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
The geometric mean of finitely many nonnegative real numbers is the nonnegative nth root of their product. For two positive numbers it is ab​. The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality compares it with their arithmetic mean. Unlike an arithmetic average, the geometric mean respects multiplicative scaling and is natural for growth factors.

Arithmetic-geometric mean iteration (an+1​=an​bn​​,bn+1​=(an​+bn​)/2)

Words: 47
Geometric mean OurBigBook.com
Starting from 0<a1​≤b1​, replace the lower endpoint by the geometric mean and the upper endpoint by the arithmetic mean. The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives an​≤an+1​≤bn+1​≤bn​. The bounded monotone sequence theorem gives limits, and the arithmetic recurrence forces them to coincide. The limiting value is the arithmetic-geometric mean of the initial pair.

Natural number (N)

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
The natural numbers are the nonnegative integers 0,1,2,….

Well-ordering principle for the natural numbers (S⊆N, S=∅⇒minS exists)

Words: 45
Natural number OurBigBook.com
Every nonempty subset of the natural numbers has a least element in their usual order. Applying this principle to positive integer linear combinations proves Bézout's identity. This principle for the usual natural-number order is distinct from the general well-ordering theorem asserting that every set can be equipped with some well-order.

Real number (R)

Words: 125 Articles: 5
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
A real number is an element of the complete ordered field R.

Archimedean property (∀x∈R ∃n∈N: n>x)

Words: 40
Real number OurBigBook.com
The Archimedean property says that the natural numbers are unbounded in the real numbers. In particular, for every positive real number a there is a positive integer n with 1/n<a. Otherwise a purported upper bound for all natural numbers contradicts the least-upper-bound property by translating that bound by one.

Harmonic mean (H=n/(∑i​1/xi​))
Words: 22
Arithmetic mean OurBigBook.com
The harmonic mean of positive numbers x1​,…,xn​ is H=n/(∑i​1/xi​). The Jensen inequality for 1/x gives H≤x, with equality exactly when all entries coincide.
Prefix sum (Pm​=∑i=1m​ai​)
Words: 30
Sum OurBigBook.com
The prefix sums Pm​=∑i=1m​ai​ can all be computed by the recurrence Pm​=Pm−1​+am​ in linear time. Any contiguous sum is then Pb​−Pa−1​, so it takes constant time after preprocessing.

Multiplication (×)

Words: 170 Articles: 5
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
Multiplication combines two factors into their product.

Product of numbers (∏i=1n​ai​)

Words: 36
Multiplication OurBigBook.com
The product of numbers a1​,…,an​ is the result of their iterated multiplication. The empty product is 1, the multiplicative identity. For positive factors, log(∏i​ai​)=∑i​logai​, turning a multiplicative conservation law into an additive derivative identity.

Exponentiation (ab)

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Multiplication OurBigBook.com
For a nonnegative integer exponent, exponentiation iterates multiplication: a0=1 and ab+1=aab. This convention defines 00=1 in primitive recursive arithmetic. Extensions to other exponents may use different domains and conventions.

Hyperoperation (a[n]b)

Words: 53
Exponentiation OurBigBook.com
The hyperoperation hierarchy successively iterates basic arithmetic operations. In the usual indexing, successor is followed by addition, multiplication, exponentiation and their higher iterates. A sequence beginning with addition shifts this index by one. Each fixed rank is a primitive recursive function; this does not imply that the evaluator taking the rank as an additional variable is primitive recursive.

Empty product (∏i∈∅​ai​=1)

Words: 35
Multiplication OurBigBook.com
A product over the empty set has value one, the identity for multiplication. This makes splitting a product into successive pieces valid even when one piece contains no factors. In particular, the factorial convention is 0!=1.

Multiplicative inverse (x−1)

Words: 12
Multiplication OurBigBook.com
A multiplicative inverse of x is an element x−1 satisfying xx−1=x−1x=1.

Arithmetic progression

Words: 127 Articles: 3
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic progression is a sequence a,a+r,…,a+(m−1)r with constant successive difference r. It is nonconstant when r=0.

Dyadic block obstruction to infinite arithmetic progressions (χ(n)=⌊log2​n⌋mod2)

Words: 50
Arithmetic progression OurBigBook.com
Colour each interval [2j,2j+1)∩N by the parity of j. Every infinite arithmetic progression of positive common difference d meets every sufficiently large such interval, since the interval has length greater than d. Both colours occur infinitely often. Thus neither colour class contains an infinite arithmetic progression, despite the finite-length conclusion of the Van der Waerden theorem.

Lifting a short modular progression to an integer progression

Words: 46
Arithmetic progression OurBigBook.com
If all residues of a modular arithmetic progression have integer representatives in an interval of diameter less than half the modulus, the representatives form an integer arithmetic progression. Consecutive differences lie in an interval shorter than the modulus, so the common modular difference has a unique possible integer representative.

Common difference

Words: 12
Arithmetic progression OurBigBook.com
The common difference of an arithmetic progression is the fixed difference between consecutive terms.

Non-Archimedean analysis

Words: 10k Articles: 215
Arithmetic OurBigBook.com
Non-Archimedean analysis studies fields whose distance is induced by an ultrametric absolute value, especially local fields and valued function fields.

Continuous functions on the p-adic integers (C(Zp​,Qp​))

Words: 567 Articles: 7
Non-Archimedean analysis OurBigBook.com
The continuous functions from the p-adic integers to the P-adic numbers form a Banach space over Qp​ with supremum norm ∥f∥∞​=supx∈Zp​​∣f(x)∣p​. Compactness of the domain bounds the norm, and uniform convergence in the complete codomain proves completeness. Translation and the forward difference operator Δf(x)=f(x+1)−f(x) are bounded operators, with ∥Δf∥∞​≤∥f∥∞​.

Mahler's theorem (f(x)=∑n≥0​an​(nx​))

Words: 527 Articles: 6
Continuous functions on the p-adic integers OurBigBook.com
Every function in continuous functions on the p-adic integers has a unique uniformly convergent expansion in the binomial polynomials, with an​→0 and an​=(Δnf)(0). Conversely, any coefficient sequence tending to zero defines such a continuous function. To prove the expansion once an​→0 is known, use ∣(nx​)∣p​≤1 for uniform convergence. Finite binomial inversion gives agreement with f at each nonnegative integer, and density gives agreement everywhere. The coefficients recover successively from these integer values, proving uniqueness. Moreover ∥f∥∞​=supn​∣an​∣p​, because finite differences bound each coefficient by the norm and the expansion gives the reverse inequality.
Discrete antidifferentiation on the p-adic integers (Jf(x)=∑n≥0​an​(f)(n+1x​))
Words: 228 Articles: 1
Mahler's theorem OurBigBook.com
The Mahler coefficients tend to zero, so the displayed series defines a continuous function and has value zero at zero. The Pascal's identity and uniform convergence give ΔJf=f. Thus the forward difference operator is surjective on continuous functions on the p-adic integers. Its kernel consists of constants: period one implies agreement on the dense nonnegative integers, and continuity then implies constancy. This selects the unique discrete antiderivative vanishing at zero.
There is also a direct construction on locally constant functions. If h has period M=pr, put aj​=h(j), S=∑i=0M−1​ai​, and Pj​=∑i<j​ai​. For x=j+My with 0≤j<M and y∈Zp​, set
Jh(x)=yS+Pj​.
(3)
This is a continuous function on each residue class. Increasing j gives Jh(x+1)−Jh(x)=aj​; at j=M−1, the next point has residue zero and quotient y+1, giving the same identity. The ultrametric inequality gives ∥Jh∥∞​≤∥h∥∞​, and Jh(0)=0. The construction is independent of the chosen period, since two normalized discrete antiderivatives agree on the nonnegative integers and then on the p-adic integers by continuity. It is linear on the locally constant functions, which form a dense subset in the supremum norm. Completeness therefore extends it to every continuous function, retaining ΔJ=I and the norm bound. This proves surjectivity without first using the Mahler theorem.
Translation-invariant linear forms on p-adic continuous functions vanish (T=0)
Words: 48
Discrete antidifferentiation on the p-adic integers OurBigBook.com
Let T:C(Zp​,Qp​)→Qp​ be linear and invariant under translation by one. For any f, choose its continuous discrete antiderivative Jf. Then T(f)=T(ΔJf)=T(Jf(⋅+1))−T(Jf)=0. No continuity or boundedness of T is assumed. In particular this applies to a form invariant under every translation by a p-adic integer.
Mahler coefficient (an​=(Δnf)(0))
Words: 212 Articles: 3
Mahler's theorem OurBigBook.com
For a continuous function f:Zp​→Qp​, its nth Mahler coefficient is
an​=∑j=0n​(−1)n−j(jn​)f(j).
(4)
This is the explicit iterate of the forward difference operator. These coefficients are exactly those of its Mahler expansion.
Mahler coefficient exponential generating function (∑n≥0​cn​Tn/n!=e−T∑n≥0​f(n)Tn/n!)
Words: 49
Mahler coefficient OurBigBook.com
For the Mahler coefficients of a continuous function on the p-adic integers, finite binomial inversion gives cn​=∑j=0n​(−1)n−j(jn​)f(j). Equivalently their exponential generating function is the displayed identity in the formal power-series ring Qp​[[T]]. Each coefficient involves only finitely many terms; no claim of convergence for every p-adic value of T is needed.
Mahler expansion of the parity function ((−1)x=∑n≥0​(−2)n(nx​) on Z2​)
Words: 65
Mahler coefficient OurBigBook.com
The locally constant function equal to one on 2Z2​ and minus one on its other coset has Mahler coefficients an​=(−2)n: at nonnegative integers its values are (−1)j, so the forward difference operator multiplies it by −2. Since ∣an​∣2​=2−n and the binomial polynomials have absolute value at most one on the 2-adic integers, the series converges uniformly. The binomial theorem verifies its values on the nonnegative integers, and continuity extends the identity to the entire domain.
Automatic decay of Mahler coefficients (an​(f)⟶0)
Words: 68
Mahler coefficient OurBigBook.com
Approximate a continuous function on Zp​ uniformly by a function constant on residue classes modulo pr. On this finite space, translation S satisfies Spr=I, so Δpr=(S−I)pr has every matrix coefficient divisible by p. Frobenius conjugacy class OurBigBook.com
Let a monic integer polynomial have distinct roots in its splitting field. Outside the finitely many primes dividing its polynomial discriminant or ramifying in that field, its roots reduce to distinct residue roots. The Frobenius automorphism permutes them by a↦ap; a reduced root belongs to Fp​ exactly when it is fixed. Distinctness of reduction identifies this with a fixed root of the Galois permutation itself. Combining this observation with a derangement in a transitive group action and the Chebotarev density theorem proves that an irreducible polynomial of degree at least two has rootless reduction at a positive Dirichlet density of primes. The degree bound is essential: every monic linear integer polynomial has a root modulo every prime.

Quadratic Hilbert symbol OurBigBook.com
For nonzero a,b in a number field, the product of their quadratic Hilbert symbols over all places is one. All but finitely many symbols are one. Over Q, this is equivalent to quadratic reciprocity with its supplementary laws. It supplies the compatibility relation between the local invariants of a global quadratic form.
Local Artin map (ArtK​)
Words: 170 Articles: 2
Local Artin reciprocity OurBigBook.com
The local Artin map is the reciprocity homomorphism of Local Artin reciprocity. Its normalization is fixed by choosing whether a uniformizer maps to arithmetic or geometric Frobenius.
Cup-product construction of local reciprocity (Gab ⌣uL/K​ ​K×/NL/K​(L×))
Words: 70
Local Artin map OurBigBook.com
For G=Gal(L/K), Tate cohomology of a finite group identifies the source as H−2(G,Z) and the target as H0(G,L×). Cup product with the local fundamental class is an isomorphism; its inverse is the finite Local Artin map. The algebraic cup-product isomorphism applies because every subgroup has first cohomology zero by Hilbert theorem 90, and second cohomology cyclic of order equal to its size by the local Brauer invariant. Compatibility with restriction and corestriction yields the tower and norm compatibility of Local Artin reciprocity.
Lubin–Tate description of local reciprocity (ArtK​(πmu)∣Kπ​​=[u−1],ArtK​(πmu)∣Knr​=FrobKm​)
Words: 76
Local Artin map OurBigBook.com
With the arithmetic Frobenius normalization, a chosen uniformizer π and Lubin–Tate formal group give these actions on the Lubin–Tate tower and the maximal unramified extension. The two fields are linearly disjoint and their compositum is the maximal abelian extension. The inverse on units is essential: using geometric Frobenius would invert the entire Local Artin map. The finite kernels on a compositum of residue degree d and torsion level r are πdZ(1+πrOK​). They are a basis of finite-index open subgroups, yielding the profinite completion of K× as the abelian Galois group.
Norm subgroup of a local field extension (NL/K​(L×))
Words: 320 Articles: 5
Local Artin reciprocity OurBigBook.com
For a finite extension of local fields L/K, its norm subgroup is the image of the field norm NL/K​:L×→K×. For an abelian extension, it is the kernel of the induced local Artin map to Gal(L/K).
Surjectivity of unit norms in unramified extensions (NL/K​(OL×​)=OK×​)
Words: 113
Norm subgroup of a local field extension OurBigBook.com
For a finite unramified extension of non-Archimedean local fields, the field norm on residue units is surjective: on a cyclic group of order qn−1 it is exponentiation by (qn−1)/(q−1) and has image of order q−1. For a common uniformizer π and r≥1, expansion of the conjugate product gives
NL/K​(1+πra)≡1+πrTrkL​/kK​​(aˉ)(modπr+1).
(47)
The field trace of a finite finite field extension is onto: its polynomial X+Xq+⋯+Xqn−1 is nonzero of degree below qn, so defines a nonzero linear map to the base field. Lift a residue norm and correct successively with elements of 1+πrOL​. The infinite product converges by completeness, and its norm is the prescribed unit. This argument also works in positive characteristic and when p divides n.
Cyclic local norm index ([K×:NL/K​L×]=[L:K])
Words: 45
Norm subgroup of a local field extension OurBigBook.com
For a cyclic extension of p-adic fields, the Herbrand quotient of the local multiplicative group together with Hilbert theorem 90 gives this index. If the ramification index and residue degree are e,f, the norm valuation formula vK​(Nx)=fvL​(x) then gives the unit norm index e. In particular all units are norms in an unramified extension.
Norm-unit index in an abelian local extension
Words: 33
Norm subgroup of a local field extension OurBigBook.com
If L/K is a finite abelian extension of local fields, then
[OK×​:NL/K​(OL×​)]=e(L/K).
(48)
Indeed, Local Artin reciprocity gives total norm index [L:K]=ef, while the valuation image of the norm subgroup is fZ.
Norm units in a tamely totally ramified extension
Words: 47
Norm subgroup of a local field extension OurBigBook.com
For a tamely totally ramified extension of degree q−1 of a local field with residue field Fq​, the unit norms are exactly the principal units. Reduction sends a unit norm to its (q−1)st power, and the norm-unit index in an abelian local extension shows that this containment has the correct index.
Norm subgroup of a 2-power cyclotomic extension of the 2-adic numbers (NQ2​(ζ2n​)/Q2​​(Q2​(ζ2n​)×))
Words: 45
Norm subgroup of a local field extension OurBigBook.com
For every positive integer n,
NQ2​(ζ2n​)/Q2​​(Q2​(ζ2n​)×)=2Z(1+2nZ2​).
(49)
Under Local Artin reciprocity, the cyclotomic character identifies the quotient with (Z/2nZ)×: a uniformizer acts trivially on the totally ramified extension, while a 2-adic unit acts through its residue class modulo 2n.
